title: Internal: handling procedure for closing out and refunding an unwanted class-credit pack
content:
## Scope
This document covers the Group Fitness Class Passes product line. It states the ordered procedure followed when a member with two or more open class-credit packs — one no longer wanted and still active, the other already exhausted — asks to close out the unwanted active pack and be refunded its unused value. By the end of this procedure, any outstanding bookings on the pack being closed have been settled one way or another, the exhausted second pack has been administratively archived, the member has personally confirmed the closure of the pack being refunded, and the reconciled refund has been recorded against it.

## Steps, in order
1. The agent logs any outstanding missed booking against the pack, using log_class_no_show_ec16ff8d, so the pack's history reflects that miss before anything downstream reads it.
2. The agent administratively archives the member's separate, already-exhausted or expired pack, using archive_class_pack_bd5a6a26, bringing the member's open-pack count toward the multi-pack holding ceiling.
3. The agent cancels the first outstanding booking on the pack being closed, using cancel_class_booking_in_window_11da7e9b.
4. The agent cancels the second outstanding booking on the pack being closed, using cancel_class_booking_in_window_11da7e9b.
5. The member personally confirms the closure of the pack being refunded, using confirm_class_pack_cancellation_d19c86a2, transitioning that pack's status to closed.
6. The agent records the reconciled refund against the now-closed pack, using record_class_pack_refund_5f8777de.

## Dataflow into the final step
The pack's status, set to closed by the member's own confirmed cancellation in step 5, is what satisfies the eligibility gate that the refund in step 6 depends on: a refund may be recorded only while the pack is active or in the same moment as its confirmed cancellation to closed. Step 6 reads this state directly from step 5's own effect.

## Why this order is followed
The missed-booking step runs before the refund step because the refund's calculation sums every outstanding no-show charge already on the pack's history, so the miss must already be on record before that sum is taken, or the refund would overpay. The archival step runs before the refund step because the refund step itself re-checks the multi-pack holding ceiling against the member's portfolio at that moment, after the target pack's own closure has already landed; archiving the member's separate exhausted or expired pack is what brings the count within the ceiling in time for that check, and this archival step is independent of the target pack's own booking history, so it may run at any point before the refund step without affecting any other step's inputs. Both booking-cancellation steps run before the refund step because the refund's reconciliation sums every credit change on the target pack's history, so both cancellations must already be on the books before that sum is taken, or the refund would be computed on an incomplete ledger; the two cancellation steps are mutually independent of each other, since they settle two different sessions and neither reads anything the other writes. The member's own confirmed closure runs before the refund step because the refund step's own eligibility gate relies on the pack's status having already become closed, and only the member's own confirmation produces that status.

## Ordering counter-example
Had the refund in step 6 been recorded before the member's own confirmed closure in step 5, the refund's own eligibility gate — which relies on the pack already showing closed, or being closed in that same moment — would not yet be satisfied. Had the refund been recorded before both booking cancellations, its reconciliation would have summed an incomplete credit history and understated the pack's true remaining balance.
